crime: Every evening, while the dining hall still stood empty, {WITCH_NAME} opened her picture book on the table and stepped inside. By the time anyone sat down, she was a small figure sitting still under its painted tree while the table talked.

One girl always left supper early to light the lounge fireplace, then read a picture book aloud by the fire while {WITCH_NAME} listened as a tiny figure in her own book, propped on the arm of the sofa. The story had a little girl in it, and whenever the little girl's line came, the reader stopped and waited for {WITCH_NAME} to say it. The whole fireside turned to the tiny figure until someone giggled.
At school, {WITCH_NAME} had once read her line aloud just as the next girl began hers. The class laughed, and the teacher skipped her turn ever after.
One night the reader told her to read that line herself tomorrow, from the sofa, not from inside the book.

The next evening, the prisoners ate supper around her small figure under the painted tree. During that supper, she stood in the lounge doorway and shot the reader in the back with a crossbow as she knelt to light the fire. Afterward the others found the reader dead at the hearth, the bolt in her back, the fire still burning. {WITCH_NAME} walked in last with her book shut under her arm, as if she had just climbed out of it.

In the trial court, the prisoners ruled her out. "She sat in her book at our table all through supper." When the court turned to her and waited for her to speak, she stepped into her book, open on the stand. On the facing page, one prisoner noticed a faint grey mirror image of a small seated girl. The court understood: the girl under the tree at supper had only been drawn in pencil. {WITCH_NAME} had never been inside.
fields.epitaph: No one will ever stop and wait for her line again.
fields.epithet: The guest who only ever showed up inside a picture
execution: The execution stand raised a tall iron frame with a glass front. She was chained upright inside it. On the glass, a fireside of listeners had been painted, every one of them turned toward her.
Paint poured from the frame's top rail and rose up the glass over her, past her knees, her waist, her chest. It closed over her mouth and nose while every painted face waited.
Then the frame hung full and still: a finished picture of listeners turned toward a small girl gone dark with paint.

magic.name: Into the Picture
magic.text: She can step bodily into paintings, drawings and photographs and walk the scene as a tiny figure.
